question_text: What is a Schottky diode, and what are its main advantages and disadvantages compared to a standard PN junction diode?
answer_text: A Schottky diode uses a metal-semiconductor junction instead of a P-N junction. It is prized for its low forward voltage drop and fast switching speed.
explanation_text:
Advantages: It has a much lower forward voltage drop (typically 0.2V - 0.3V compared to 0.7V for standard silicon), which heavily reduces conduction power losses (P = I * V). It also has near-zero reverse recovery time, making it excellent for high-frequency switching.
Disadvantages: It suffers from significantly higher reverse leakage current and typically has lower maximum reverse voltage ratings.
bonus_question_text: Why did the industry replace Schottky diodes with NMOS transistors in modern synchronous buck converters?
bonus_answer_text: Even with a low 0.3V drop, a Schottky diode passing 10A wastes 3 Watts of heat. A modern NMOS has ultra-low R_DS(on), wasting significantly less power (P = I^2 * R).
